label: 74HC373 8-bit Transparent D-Latch with Tri-State Output

semantics.notes: 8-bit transparent latch. LE=1: outputs follow inputs (transparent). LE=0: outputs hold. /OE (active-low): when /OE=1, all outputs go Hi-Z. When /OE=0, outputs are driven from internal state. Note: LE and /OE are independent. You can hold /OE=1 (outputs disabled) while latch is transparent or held. isSynchronous field is NOT set (falsy) — latches are level-sensitive. clockInputId=null — no timing detection.

exportSupport.verilogNotes: LE latch via always@(*). /OE tri-state via conditional assign. Verify the exact HDL pattern — may use two separate always blocks or nested conditionals.
exportSupport.vhdlNotes: Process for latch + concurrent assignment for tri-state.

testability.notes: Tests: LE=1 transparent (Q follows D changes); LE=0 hold (D changes don't affect Q); /OE=1 outputs go Hi-Z regardless of LE and Q state; /OE=0 outputs driven from latched state; combine: LE=1,/OE=1 (inputs update internal, but outputs still Hi-Z); multi-driver bus test with two 74HC373 chips and complementary /OE.

risks.description: No defaultInputValues set for /OE. Disconnected /OE=0 by default (active) — outputs driven immediately. This is the opposite-safe default vs. typical bus designs.
Does the implementation correctly combine LE (latch) and /OE (tri-state) as independent controls? Risk of incorrect coupling.
isSynchronous not set — unclear how STT treats this gate.

modelLimits: No setup/hold timing for LE vs D.
